title: 1 Chronicles 20:1–3
context: In the spring, Joab leads the army against Ammon and besieges Rabbah while David stays in Jerusalem. Joab takes the city, David receives the Ammonite crown and much plunder, and the people of the Ammonite cities are subjected. This parallels 2 Samuel 11:1 and 12:26–31. Between those verses, 2 Samuel tells the account of David, Bathsheba, and Uriah and Nathan's rebuke; the Chronicler does not include that account here.

verses.text: At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army and wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah, and overthrew it.
verses.arminianNotes: Joab besieges and overthrows Rabbah, "but David stayed at Jerusalem." Arminian readers note that this verse parallels 2 Samuel 11:1, and that the Chronicler does not include the account of David and Bathsheba that 2 Samuel places at this point.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the Chronicler moves directly from the siege to its conclusion, while 2 Samuel 12:26–29 has Joab call David to come and take the city. The omission is noted without filling it in.

verses.text: David took the crown of their king from off his head, and found it to weigh a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it. It was set on David’s head, and he brought very much plunder out of the city.
verses.arminianNotes: David takes the crown of their king, weighing a talent of gold with precious stones, and much plunder. Arminian readers note, as at 2 Samuel 12:30, that the crown's weight has led some interpreters to suggest it was worn only ceremonially.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note, consistent with the notes on 2 Samuel 12:30, that the Hebrew word rendered "their king" can also be read as Milcom, the Ammonite god. The text allows either reading.

verses.text: He brought out the people who were in it, and had them cut with saws, with iron picks, and with axes. David did so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
verses.arminianNotes: David has the people "cut with saws, with iron picks, and with axes." Arminian readers note that the parallel in 2 Samuel 12:31 reads "put them to work under saws" and mentions brick kilns; the wording differs and interpreters disagree on what is meant.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note, consistent with the notes on 2 Samuel 12:31, that the Hebrew is difficult and that forced labor or harsher treatment are both proposed. The verse is read soberly, not held up as a model.
